thread:
Keisha: Heads-up from Sales: NovaCard reporting p95 regression after last maintenance. Moving intake here to triage priority/scope. Ticket: https://support.redwood.example/t/NOVA-214
Vik: Customer on Dedicated (eu-west-1). SLA 250ms p95. Seeing ~750ms p95 spikes around 01:30-02:00 UTC. QPS steady at ~9. Model: `cardio-large-quant`.
Anil: Release notes show runtime bump to runt-2.21 and a model variant swap to `cardio-large-quant-v2`. No routing config changes on their account.
Rosa: Quick triage questions: 1) did we change batching or kernel selection defaults? 2) can Eng reproduce in staging? 3) proposed closure criteria?
Samir: Infra notes: deploy-bot reported PROD deploy runt-2.21 completed at 2026-04-15T01:13:22Z
Vik: Sales attached their latency graph. Spikes coincide with larger sequence lengths (~900-1400 tokens). p50 unchanged.
Anil: Hypotheses: (A) KV-cache warmup/preservation semantics changed in runt-2.21 for quantized variants; (B) kernel fallback for long sequences causing slow path; (C) batching timer interactions producing singleton small batches that hit slow kernels.
Keisha: For prioritization Product recommends P1: paid Dedicated customer, SLA breached. Closure/launch criteria proposal: 1) root cause identified and mitigation deployed OR rollback validated; 2) p95 <= 300ms for 2 hours under comparable traffic; 3) customer updated within 60 minutes and then hourly until stable. Agree?
Vik: Agreed. Also ask Eng to estimate rollback vs config-change time and blast radius. Product needs that to negotiate with Sales.
Anil: I can reproduce in staging with their token histogram and payload. Need a redacted recent request sample from Sales.
sales-bot: Customer provided sample (redacted): ``{"prompt":"Summarize recent cardiology notes","max_tokens":256}`` Sequence distribution: most 200-800, ~10% 900-1400.
eng-oncall-bot: Note: we currently lack CI gating that covers quantized-variant long-sequence tails. Adding to backlog recommended.
Samir: Quick mitigations: (1) config flip to preserve KV cache + bump min-ready for their pool (low blast radius) — ~20-45m to canary and validate; (2) canary rollback to runt-2.20 (fast path) — ~30-50m to canary then validate; (3) route customer to alternate pool as short term (manual) — ~15-30m but needs coordination.
Keisha: Product asks Eng to produce a short runbook listing: canary config flip steps, canary rollback steps, metrics to watch (p50/p95, kv-hit-rate, cold-start-count, kernel-fallback-rate, batch-size-dist), and customer comms template. Also create backlog ticket with acceptance test and CI gating for quantized variants.
Anil: Starting repro now at 10 qps with their token histogram. Will post flamegraphs, trace spans, and heap diffs in ~35m. If I reproduce on runt-2.21 and not on 2.20 that's a clear signal.
Vik: Sales: customer asked about SLA credits if not resolved within 24h. Please coordinate on comms; Product will give timeline once Eng estimates rollback/hotfix.
sales-bot: Noted. Customer wants hourly updates and prefers minimal disruption. They indicated they'd accept a rollback if it's quick.
Keisha: Product negotiating priorities: we have two other P1s in the sprint. If rollback is low-risk we'll agree to immediate rollback. If rollback is high-risk, propose config canary + routing fallback to buy time. Need Eng ETA for both options.
Anil: Preliminary ETA: config canary + validation ~25-40m; rollback canary ~30-45m + 20-40m to widen if canary is green. Hotfix for kernel selection bug could be 3+ hours. I'll confirm after repro.
Samir: If config flip fixes it on canary, that's preferable because it has lower blast radius. We'll still prepare rollback approval flow in parallel.
Vik: Product: please add acceptance criteria to the backlog ticket: synthetic test using `cardio-large-quant-v2`, seq tail to 1400 tokens, 10 qps for 1 hour asserting p95 < 300ms; CI gating of runtime bumps for quantized models.
eng-oncall-bot: deploy-bot: rollback-run-2319990355 created (manual approval required)
Anil: Early repro notes: p50 steady; p95 spikes correlate with traces showing `kernel_fallback=true` and low kv-hit-rate on nodes that recently received the new image. Suspect KV preservation + kernel path interplay. Posting initial traces to ticket.
Keisha: Good detail. Product asks Support to prepare a short customer update: ack + ETA 60m, mention possible config canary or rollback, reassure about SLA credit handling. I'll coordinate with Sales on tone.
Vik: Sales: customer prefers config change if it avoids routing. They asked whether we can pin their pool to the previous runtime until confirmed stable. Product: advise on pinning policy and tradeoffs.
Keisha: Pinning is an option but it's a product decision—consensus required. For immediate triage, prioritize fastest safe mitigation. Postmortem and decision on pinning after stability. We'll add pinning decision to acceptance criteria for the backlog ticket.
Samir: Action items recap: Anil -> repro + logs + recommendation (eng); Samir -> prep rollback approval (infra); Keisha -> draft customer update and coordinate with Sales (product); Vik -> open backlog ticket with ACs and gating request (product); sales-bot -> keep hourly updates to customer.
Anil: Will update thread in ~35m with artifacts. If config canary works I'll include exact config diff to apply.
Vik: Customer acknowledged receipt of initial update. :thumbsup:
Keisha: Closing intake here; continuing execution in PROD ticket REDWOOD-NOVA-214. We'll reopen thread if scope/prio changes.
